result.summary: Demotes Tor control port connection failures from unconditional warnings back to the Tor debug category. It also marks the socket connection attempt as non-manual so that underlying socket connection errors are not unconditionally logged.
result.problem: Since commit eae193e750, failed Tor control port connection and reconnection attempts log warnings unconditionally. On default-configured nodes where a Tor daemon is not running, this pollutes debug.log with approximately 18 warning lines every hour.
evidence: PR description: 'Since eae193e750 (in v32), every failed reconnect attempt logs... On a default configured node without tor, this pollutes debug.log with 18 lines every hour.'
Referenced issue #36691: 'v32.0: Connection to tor control port cannot be disabled'
result.changed_since_previous: The diff additionally changes manual_connection from true to false in ConnectDirectly, suppressing the lower-level socket error log alongside the two torcontrol LogWarning calls.
result.card: This PR demotes Tor control port connection failure messages from unconditional warnings back to the tor debug logging category. On default-configured nodes operating without a local Tor daemon, periodic reconnection attempts currently output repeated warning logs, adding roughly 18 lines of log noise to debug.log every hour. Moving both the torcontrol logs and the underlying socket connection failure to debug level stops this log spam for users not running Tor.

risk.why: A mistake in log levels or socket connection flags could hide Tor control port failures from operators troubleshooting Tor issues.
